newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh bourse refuses to list six companies.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh bourse refuses to list six companies.

text.p: The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) has refused to list six Bangladesh companies that have sold millions of dollars worth of shares to the public.
A DSE statement published in newspapers on Thursday said a DSE committee on Monday had rejected listing applications by the companies because they had failed to meet requirements set by the bourse.

It said the companies were Anlima Yarn Dyeing Ltd, Mark Bangladesh Shilpa and Engineering Ltd, HR Textile Mills Ltd, Excelsior Shoes Ltd, Meghna Vegetable Oil Industry Ltd, and First BSRS Mutual Fund.
DSE officials said the six companies had already raised more than 500 million taka ($12 million) through the selling of initial public offerings (IPOs).
"Despite repeated requests from the DSE, none of the companies submitted the papers and documents fully...," the statement said.
The DSE officials and traders said the companies had already issued allotment letters to subscribers.
"But trading on the shares could not be started because of the non-listing," said trader Mohammad Hannan.

DSE rules say each company that goes public should be listed on the bourse within six weeks of the close of the subscription. Otherwise the allotment is void and the companies should refund money received from applicants, the Financial Express said.

The newspaper said if the companies failed to refund the subscription money within 30 days after the end of the six-week period, the directors of the companies would be responsible collectively and would have to refund the money with interest.
